chunks: Among what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated, from al-Nadr, from 'Asim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who doubted regarding the first rak'ah. He said: "He starts over."

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, the one giving the ruling
key_terms.الرَّكْعَةِ الْأُولَى: the first rak'ah of the prayer
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ: the narrator transmitting the report from the Imam
key_terms.يَسْتَأْنِفُ: he restarts or begins the prayer anew

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone doubts in the first rak'ah of salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning doubt in salat (prayer), specifically when uncertainty occurs in the first rak'ah. Imam Abu Ja'far عليه السلام states that the prayer must be restarted, showing the seriousness of uncertainty at the beginning of the prayer.
